newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police break up anti-Lukashenko protest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police break up anti-Lukashenko protest.

text.p: Police beat nationalists protesting against plans to form a union between Belarus and Russia on Friday and arrested about 50 people for trying to hold an unsanctioned demonstration.

Reuters correspondents on Independence Square in the capital of the former Soviet republic saw police bundling about 50 people -- including opposition journalists and two opposition politicians -- into two trucks and several police jeeps.
Some of those arrested looked dazed but there was no sign of bloodshed as police moved in to break up a gathering of about 1,000 nationalists, intellectuals and young people.

They were voicing their opposition to President Alexander Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with neighbouring Russia, set out in a deal last year on forming a "commonwealth" of the two Slav states.

President Boris Yeltsin told Russian media chiefs on Friday that Belarus might merge altogether with Russia in the future, Interfax news agency said. "Maybe after all this will be a single state," he was quoted as saying.
Lukashenko said however the former Soviet republic had no plans for a full-scale merger.
"Belarus will remain an independent state," spokesman Valery Tolkachyov quoted Lukashenko as saying in an interview with the earlier on Friday.
Later, police used clubs and forced street protesters to the ground after instructing them several times to clear the area.
Anatoly Lebedko and Boris Gunter, members of the alternative parliament of former deputies, were arrested.
Authorities had sanctioned the rally, titled "Belarus into Europe," but they were banned from proceeding through the city.
They had planned to tour Western embassies to register their protest against Lukashenko's authoritarian rule.

Lukashenko, facing a "political spring" by opposition forces, has ordered restrictions on political rallies and banned his opponents from using post-independence national symbols, which he has scrapped in favour of old Soviet ones.
The press secretary for his policy-making Security Council, Vasily Baranov, accused the opposition of looking for a fight and of getting "more and more out of control".
The U.S. State Department accused Belarus last week of failing to uphold democracy and human rights and announced it was halting all U.S. aid to the country of 10 million.
Police arrested Professor Yuri Khodyko, 53, a leader of the Popular Front which organised the protest, in an overnight raid.
Minsk authorities have also banned protesters from marching through the capital on Saturday, when opposition forces plan a large rally to mark Constitution Day.
The republic's first constitution was rewritten by the president last November when he won a landslide victory in a controversial referendum on expanding his powers.
Opposition deputies who refused to join the two-chamber parliament created under Lukashenko's constitution were meeting at a "house of culture" outside the centre.
The European parliament still recognises the old parliament, saying the new one was formed illegally.
Opposition leaders have vowed to proceed with Saturday's protest as well despite the restrictions.
